item.title: 'Acting is doing': Willem Dafoe on what people get wrong about acting
item.description: Willem Dafoe's desire to challenge himself has made the 71-year-old very productive. He's in five films being released in the second half of this year. That includes his most recent film, Late Fame.

item.title: Nashville celebrates Dolly Parton on 9/25 in a nod to '9 to 5'
item.description: It's Sept. 25, and in a nod to "9 to 5", people in Nashville and other places are celebrating the Queen of Country, Dolly Party.

item.title: 'The Disappearers' is a fiercely personal novel that hits like a tidal wave
item.description: Marlon James' new novel chronicles the events surrounding a vicious anti-gay attack in Jamaica in the late 1980s. Shortlisted for the Booker Prize, The Disappearers churns with passion and ideas.
item.content:encoded: Marlon James' new novel chronicles the events surrounding a vicious anti-gay attack in Jamaica in the late 1980s. Shortlisted for the Booker Prize, The Disappearers churns with passion and ideas.

item.title: 'To Catch a Predator' drama 'Primetime' brings the sleaze, and it's almost enough
item.description: Primetime dramatizes the story behind the series To Catch a Predator. It's full of big swings from the director and the actors — but doesn't engage with the most complicated questions the series raised.

item.description: South Africa is aiming to smash a savory world record — the world's largest BBQ — and more boerewors sausage than you can shake a stick at.

item.title: 'Bad Boy For Life' investigates the culture that enabled Sean Combs' alleged abuse
item.description: Rolling Stone reporter Cheyenne Roundtree says rumors of abuse followed the media mogul for years. Her book examines how Combs remained so powerful, despite decades of warning signs and allegations.

item.title: Mahershala Ali stars as a devout father of three, making ends meet as a hitman
item.description: It's not easy, killing people and raising a family. The new action-thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother reaffirms the power of faith — and delights in outrageous juxtapositions.

item.title: 'Empire' asks: When a child dies, who pays the price?
item.description: Set in the same universe as Tahir's Ember in Ashes series, Empire picks up right where the last book, 'Heir' left off — with S'rsha attached to the very monster she sought to destroy.
